newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Sterling/mark braced for a test of 3.03.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Sterling/mark braced for a test of 3.03.

text.p: Sterling has its sights on a retest of 3.03 marks now that it has battered down initial resistance near 3.02 to set one-week highs, technical analysts said.
These gains will be a by-product of the dollar's rise against the mark, though, leaving cable vulnerable to a pullback to $1.6720 and lower, they said.

"It is more a case of mark weakness than anything else, but it looks like we could see another test of the day's highs and then go up to 3.03 in the next day or so," said Richard Adcock, manager of technical research at HSBC Futures.
Sterling was at 3.0212/22 at 0745 GMT from 3.0153/58 late Monday in Europe. Cable was at $1.6716/26 from $1.6768/78 yesterday.

Howard Wright, chief technical analyst at Prisma Market Analysts, is also targeting a move up to 3.03 marks, the highest sterling reached on July 15, a day after it hit the six-and-a-half-year peak of 3.0327.

Wright said he would only begin to question sterling's up move if the pound traded below the psychological 3.0 mark on a daily closing basis, something it has not done since it broke above this barrier on July 11.
"The chances of (this) taking place look to be somewhere between slim and none," he said.
Adcock at HSBC Futures expects sterling/mark to find support at the 3.0140/45 level, the high on July 16 which acted as resistance on the way up, on any retracement.
Meantime, cable is eyeing the downside, analysts said.

Chris Dunne, director at Forexia, told RFTV that he expects cable to break below the $1.6720 trendline support it has already tested this morning and to extend its losses towards $1.66. This marks congestive support from the end of June.
